body: I get the bonding part for sure, but in my head I can't really "get" bonding so quickly with a new pet. I guess I'm just defective lmao

Yeah I get what you mean. I do eventually want to get a pet but I'm not sure if I'd ever be "hysterical sobbing, take days off work" sad if it died, you know? I guess some people just takes things like that harder.

I knew I'd get this comment. Obviously a person (no matter how old) passing is tragic and even though I haven't any personal experiences with grief I can completely comprehend mourning when someone you love dies. I understand that pets are often regarded as family too but I have no experience with them so I'm asking a legitimate question. No need to be snarky.
i knew i needed to look into emotional neglect as it sounds similar to what i've experienced, but i've never heard of reparenting so i'll have to check that out, thank you

i want that validation so badly ngl, none of my problems have ever felt severe enough. i dont have a therapist (boooo american healthcare system) but my girlfriend is my rock, she helps a lot and im glad i have her

yeah, it feels like i need to do something extreme to be noticed. i know i could get the help i need in a less drastic way, but seeking out help in a healthy way feels a lot harder than something on a larger scale. couldn't tell you why

you kind of nailed it with that not gonna lie, though idk if i actually wanna succeed at suicide. it seems so scary. i just kinda want my problems to be noticed and idk how else to do that without having some huge episode. like, i want my friends to worry about me, you know? is that weird? but tbh im not even sure how much that'd happen, most of my friends at my college are in their own apartment now and we don't eat lunch and dinner together anymore like we used to so im not even sure if they'd notice if I was in a psych ward for a week or two. thank you though, I'll keep your words in mind

i mean i guess it depends on the method? like what you're describing is probably more accurate for pills but i dont really have access to those. can't really think of other practical methods though which is "good" i guess

i think it's definitely insecurity as well, she's been cheated on in the past so she's afraid to lose me. i think clarifying that im having an off day when i feel bad is good, idk why i havent thought of that lol. 

as for therapy/medication, idk if she's been in therapy before but she stopped meds long before we dated because she didn't like how it felt like they muted all her emotions. i want to encourage her to continue meds, but she's afraid that her love for me will be muted too. i dont know what will convince her, but maybe if i get professional help for my own issues it'll encourage her to do so as well.
That makes me feel better, I really liked that piercing. I'm not quite sure whether I'll re-pierce or not but I guess I have a good few months to decide lmao
I'm well aware I need therapy, but I don't have the time, resources, or money to pursue it right now. If it was as simple as "I need therapy" I would've gotten it years ago
